name: Throwing Muses
label: 4AD
lede: Two step-sisters from Newport, Rhode Island started a band as high school freshmen and became the first Americans on 4AD. Kristin Hersh is still making Muses records forty-odd years later.

eras.title: Freshmen in Newport
eras.text: Kristin Hersh and Tanya Donelly became step-sisters when Donelly's father married Hersh's mother, and at 14 Hersh talked Donelly into a band. Through high school and Salve Regina it grew from Kristin Hersh and the Muses into Throwing Muses, with a drummer who'd never sat at a kit.

years.src: Wikipedia: Kristin Hersh · Wikipedia: Throwing Muses
years.h: Hersh, 14, talks Donelly into starting the Muses
years.p: The first line-up has Elaine Adamedes on bass and Becca Blumen on drums. Both sisters are freshmen at Rogers High School in Newport.

years.big: "I learned to play on it without cymbals."
years.h: David Narcizo replaces Becca Blumen on drums
years.p: Narcizo had only played marching and concert drums. The cymbal-free kit became his trademark.
years.xp:
His full account: "I had never played a drum kit before, all I'd played was marching drums and concert drums." He'd stay for the whole run and every reunion.

He came in after hearing Hersh play piano.

years.h: A car hits Hersh while she's cycling
years.p: Hersh, 16, suffers a double concussion. She has described the sounds she heard afterward turning into syllables and drums, the start of how songs came to her.

years.h: The first EP comes out on the band's own Blowing Fuses label
years.p: The self-titled EP is a homemade release from the Newport years.

years.h: Gary Smith at Fort Apache records the Doghouse Cassette
years.p: The demos, cut with Smith at the Boston-area studio, get to 4AD. [[Leslie Langston|5d9bb2c3-a707-4ef7-a7a3-8fb74776b255]] has replaced Adamedes on bass.

eras.title: Boston, Gil Norton and the Pixies as support
eras.text: Signing to 4AD in 1986 moved a British label toward America. The band relocated to Boston, made a debut Spin gave a 10, and took a new local band called Pixies on tour as their support.

years.cap: Live at Kendall Co-op, Cambridge, Massachusetts
years.src: Wikipedia: Throwing Muses · Wikipedia: Tanya Donelly · Wikipedia: 4AD · Perfect Sound Forever · The Quietus
years.h: 4AD signs its first American band
years.p: The Doghouse Cassette reaches [[Ivo Watts-Russell|cf86cec1-1baf-4d8a-ba1e-01568332585a]], who starts phoning the band's Boston apartment.
years.xp: Watts-Russell told them at first that he 'didn't sign American bands', then signed them anyway. Hersh's reason for saying yes: 'I signed with them because Ivo was funny and goofy, and that was about it.'

years.h: Gil Norton produces the debut, and Spin gives it a 10
years.p: Hersh writes every song but Donelly's Green. Pitchfork later scored it 9.2.
years.xp: Recorded between December 1985 and June 1986. Norton would go on to produce Pixies. The album fell out of print in the early 1990s and came back in 1998 on the 4AD/Rykodisc set In a Doghouse, with the Chains Changed EP, the early demos and the band's award-winning video for Fish.

years.src: Wikipedia: Throwing Muses · Wikipedia: House Tornado
years.h: The Fat Skier follows Chains Changed
years.p: Two EPs in one year. 4AD's CD of the next album adds all six Fat Skier tracks; the American edition leaves them off.

years.cap: Sire's US poster for House Tornado, 1988
years.h: Sire swaps 4AD's collage for a band photo on House Tornado
years.p: Recorded at Fort Apache with Gary Smith and Paul Q. Kolderie. In the US it's on Sire Records, which pushes the band hard.
years.xp: Hersh in 2011: 'It's a universe. It's when we were still allowed to be on our own planet.'

years.cap: Throwing Muses and Pixies together for Melody Maker, May 1988
years.src: Wikipedia: Throwing Muses · Guardian: Kristin Hersh · The Quietus
years.h: Pixies open for the Muses across the UK
years.p: The two Boston bands tour Britain together from late April, with the Muses headlining.
years.xp: Hersh first heard Pixies at a soundcheck, when a painter friend at the bar told her to listen. She thought Charles Thompson was a woman at first, and decided on the spot: 'You're playing all of our shows with us.' Her manager and label came with the offer.

years.h: Hunkpapa edges toward rock and Dizzy gets on US alternative radio
years.p: Dizzy reaches No. 8 on the US alternative chart; the album reaches No. 59 in the UK. Donelly co-writes Dragonhead and Angel.
years.xp: The New York Times heard the band edging toward rock convention; the Rolling Stone Album Guide liked the stronger groove. Robert Christgau called it an improvement, just not the difference that would make the difference.

years.h: Donelly and Kim Deal make Pod as [[The Breeders|667e856e-f3a7-42e9-8244-95422ef31321]]
years.p: The side project with the Pixies bassist puts out its debut. Donelly drifts away after the 1992 Safari EP.

years.src: Wikipedia: Throwing Muses · Wikipedia: Red Heaven
years.h: Fred Abong takes over from Leslie Langston on bass
years.p: Langston leaves before the fourth album. She'll come back as a guest on Red Heaven.

eras.title: Donelly's songs leave with her
eras.text: The Real Ramona was the last record with two songwriters. Within months Donelly had a band of her own and the Muses were down to three.

years.cap: Hersh, Donelly, Narcizo and Abong at Wax'n'Facts, Atlanta, June 1991
years.h: Dennis Herring takes The Real Ramona to Los Angeles
years.p: It reaches No. 26 in the UK and Select gives it five out of five. Donelly's Not Too Soon is a single alongside Counting Backwards.
years.xp: Recorded July to November 1990 at London and Dust Bowl studios in LA. Donelly wrote Not Too Soon and Honeychain. NME named it the 35th best album of 1991.

years.src: Wikipedia: Throwing Muses · Wikipedia: Tanya Donelly
years.h: Donelly leaves to start [[Belly|c118bc97-11a7-41dc-a55e-48c3bcf22ac2]] and takes Abong with her
years.p: Belly's 1993 debut Star reaches No. 2 in the UK, and Feed the Tree tops the US Modern Rock chart and draws two Grammy nominations.

eras.title: The roadie plays bass
eras.text: As a trio, with former roadie Bernard Georges on bass, the Muses made their highest-charting record and then lost their major label. Hersh had a solo career running alongside by now.

years.cap: Hersh at the Borderline, London, July 1992
years.src: Wikipedia: Red Heaven · Wikipedia: Throwing Muses
years.h: Bob Mould duets on Dio on Red Heaven
years.p: The first album as a trio, with Georges on bass and Langston guesting. It's No. 13 in the UK and they tour it with [[The Flaming Lips|1f43d76f-8edf-44f6-aaf1-b65f05ad9402]].
years.xp: Cut January to May 1992 at Fort Apache and the Power Station in New York, co-produced with Steve Boyer. [[Bob Mould|d7f5305a-15fc-4af4-a61b-f6f45510cc8f]] of [[Hüsker Dü|5c4c90a4-539f-4101-83cf-301bc6a94e06]] sings on Dio. The UK limited edition came with a live CD from Maxwell's in Hoboken.

years.h: Hersh's solo Hips and Makers goes first
years.p: [[Michael Stipe|905a8f9b-03dc-4f47-b9bb-ecce7ea13ab1]] of [[R.E.M.|ea4dfa26-f633-4da6-a52a-f49ea4897b58]] sings on it. The finished Muses album waits until it's out.

years.h: Bright Yellow Gun is their first US hit, and Sire lets them go
years.p: University, recorded at Kingsway in New Orleans, reaches No. 10 in the UK. US sales disappoint Sire, which drops the band.
years.xp: Hersh has her own version of the exit: 'I bought myself out of my contract by trading them my first solo record for my freedom.' She also says Sire 'never lifted a finger to sell Muse's records.'

years.h: Gilbert Hernandez of Love and Rockets draws Limbo
years.p: Back in New Orleans, with Trina Shoemaker engineering, the band makes its Rykodisc album. Shark reaches No. 53 in the UK.

years.src: Wikipedia: Limbo · Wikipedia: David Narcizo · Wikipedia: Kristin Hersh · Perfect Sound Forever
years.h: Throwing Muses stop, and Hersh goes solo
years.p: Narcizo starts the electronic project Lakuna with his wife Melissa; Georges keeps playing with Hersh. Hersh and Billy O'Connell had started the ThrowingMusic label in 1996.
years.xp: Hersh doesn't call it a split: 'I don't think we ever broke up; we just don't always have the money.'

eras.title: Purgatory Road, Paradise Avenue
eras.text: The trio came back in 2003 and has put records out every several years since, on its own schedule. Hersh's other band, 50 Foot Wave, and her books ran alongside.

years.cap: Hersh and Donelly at the Middle East, Cambridge, Massachusetts, April 2003
years.src: Wikipedia: Throwing Muses (2003 · Wikipedia: David Narcizo · The Quietus
years.h: A second self-titled album, out the same day as Hersh's The Grotto
years.p: Cut over three weekends in 2002 and paid for with Hersh's solo advance, with Donelly on backing vocals on five songs. NME gives it 8 out of 10, and the trio tours Europe and the US.

years.h: Hersh's memoir Rat Girl goes back to 1985
years.p: It covers the year of the 4AD deal and the debut, alongside her bipolar diagnosis, her first pregnancy and her friendship with the actress Betty Hutton. In the UK it's Paradoxical Undressing.
years.xp: Rob Sheffield, reviewing it for the New York Times, called it sensitive and raw and also wildly funny. Rolling Stone put it at No. 8 on its 2012 list of the greatest rock memoirs.

years.cap: Hersh, Narcizo and Georges in San Francisco
years.src: Wikipedia: Purgatory · Wikipedia: Throwing Muses · The Paris Review
years.h: Thirty-two tracks, sold as a book
years.p: Purgatory/Paradise comes as a book of lyrics and art with a download code. The title is two crossing roads in Middletown, Rhode Island.
years.xp:
The band produced it themselves, with Steve Rizzo engineering and Bhob Rainey mixing. Pitchfork gave it 8.0. Early in 2014 the Muses toured select US cities, with Donelly opening the East Coast dates.

The 32 songs were cut down from about 75, made over five years with money from listeners. Narcizo on the sound: 'This one is more delicate. It sits down next to you.'

years.h: Sun Racket, written in what Hersh calls a fugue state
years.p: The first Muses album in seven years, on Fire Records, scores 83 on Metacritic. Hersh says she has no memory of writing the songs.

years.h: A cello joins the Muses on Moonlight Concessions
years.p: Pete Harvey plays cello on songs Hersh wrote across the Gulf Coast and Southern California. It reaches No. 5 on the UK indie chart; the Guardian gives it four stars.
